gaps.sentence: He isn't old ___ to drive a car.
gaps.explanation: 'Old enough' means sufficiently old; 'enough' follows the adjective, while 'too' gives the opposite meaning.
'Too cold to swim' means the temperature prevents swimming; 'enough' would follow the adjective.

gaps.sentence: He took ___ notice of the warning and carried on as before.
gaps.explanation: 'Take little notice of' means to pay hardly any attention; 'notice' is uncountable here.

gaps.sentence: Every one of the switches ___ been tested twice.
gaps.explanation: 'Every one of' takes a singular verb: has.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the workforce is part-time now.
gaps.hint: pattern: ___ of + specific group; singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Half of the workforce is ...' is the correct pattern; 'the half of' is not used in this position.

gaps.sentence: There's ___ point in complaining — no one will listen.
gaps.hint: fixed expression: ___ point in doing something
gaps.explanation: 'There's little point in doing something' means it is hardly worth doing; 'point' is uncountable here.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the students has been given a personal timetable.
gaps.hint: this is the only option that can be followed by 'of' and take a singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Each of the students has ...' is correct; 'every' cannot take 'of' here and 'all/both' need a plural verb.

gaps.sentence: He's lucky: he has ___ good friends he can rely on.
gaps.hint: positive meaning with a countable plural
gaps.explanation: 'A few' means some — a positive idea — and is used with countable plurals like friends.
